Open-weight wave (the thesis stopped being an argument: Mozilla's report shows OpenRouter traffic flipped from 60/40 closed-favoring to 63/37 open-favoring in four months, with open-model throughput up ~5x to 4.19T tokens/day - the same day Kimi K3 (2.8T) and Inkling (975B, Apache 2.0) both landed. Inkling's pitch is the business model: open base plus hosted Tinker fine-tuning, so an enterprise can own a model that beats frontier on its own tasks)

Frontier models - open Chinese (Kimi K3's real numbers land: 2.8T sparse MoE with 16 of 896 experts active, Kimi Delta Attention, 1M context, native vision, priced $3/$15 - the highest of any Chinese lab but roughly half the per-task cost of Opus 4.8. In blind Arena testing developers preferred it over every leading US model for front-end coding, including Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol. The weights don't drop until July 27, so nobody outside Moonshot has inspected them)

Open-weight cost pressure (two frontier-scale open releases in 24h — Thinking Machines' Inkling, a 975B/41B-active Apache-2.0 MoE at ~41 on the AA Index and the strongest US open-weights model yet, and Moonshot's Kimi K3 at 2.8T the largest ever — as Mozilla's data shows OpenRouter flipped 63/37 to open; Nathan Lambert's '6 months to live' warns a White House EO could close the window)

Chinese / open frontier models (Moonshot's Kimi K3 takes the size crown from DeepSeek V4 at 2.8T params, lands #1 on the Frontend Code Arena and goes live at $3/$15 ahead of Jul-27 weights; DeepSeek V4 exits preview with peak-hour pricing — the open-weight release cadence out of China keeps compressing the gap despite export controls)

Open-weight cost pressure (Kimi K3 at $3/$15 keeps compressing the gap to closed US labs; Thinking Machines' 975B Inkling stands as the leading US open-weights counterweight; Ollama repositions around 'All Aboard Open Models' — the open-weight cadence is now the frontier's pace-setter two weeks before EU GPAI fines)

Chinese / open frontier models (Moonshot's 2.8T Kimi K3 dominates the weekend as a geopolitics story — #1 on the Frontend Code Arena, 93.5% GPQA, open weights promised Jul 27; Alibaba's Qwen 3.8 lands as a rushed answer with a hosted Max preview; commenters count 12+ providers claiming >Opus 4.5 and expect DeepSeek V4 'final' imminently)

Open-weight cost pressure (Nathan Lambert's 'Kimi K3 escalation' puts the open->closed and American->Chinese gap at 3-5 months, down from 6-9; Kimi K3 at $3/$15 and Qwen3.8-Max's ~10% preview pricing keep compressing it, and Fireworks' $1.5B Series D at $17.5B capitalizes the layer that serves open weights in production)

Evaluation gap ('Beyond Final Scores' and QuoteBench make the same argument from opposite ends — end scores hide how long-horizon agents behave, and two models with identical benchmark numbers can fail very differently on the command path; HN supplies the field evidence, calling Bullet's benchmark saturated enough to be meaningless and noting neither Ultrafast post states that quality matches standard 5.6 Sol)
